item.content:encoded:
‎The predicted onset of El Nino may lead to urban migration and social issues in the island communities of Lousiade in Samarai-Murua as the dry spell prolongs. ‎ As the prolonged dry spell continues, families in rural island communities in the Lousiade local level government may be forced to leave their homes and migrate to urban areas in search of food, water and better living conditions. ‎ ‎Lousiade LLG president Solomon Paulisbo said he dreads social issues could emerge once the full impact of the El Nino sets in Milne Bay.

“People will be forced to look for comforts in the urban areas, and they do that we are looking at social issues,” he said.

Paulisbo said they've established plans to respond to the El Nino effects but to date, they still haven't received any funding from the disaster relief components to implement their plans. ‎

item.title: Police launch manhunt for 16 escapees in Enga
item.description: A police operation is underway in Enga to recapture 16 remand prisoners who escaped from the Wabag Police Station lock-up early on Wednesday morning. Enga provincial police commander Chief Supt Steven Harris confirmed that of the 16 escapees, nine had been refused police bail and were awaiting court appearances when they broke out on July 29.
item.content:encoded:
A police operation is underway in Enga to recapture 16 remand prisoners who escaped from the Wabag Police Station lock-up early on Wednesday morning.

Enga provincial police commander Chief Supt Steven Harris confirmed that of the 16 escapees, nine had been refused police bail and were awaiting court appearances when they broke out on July 29.

Chief Supt Harris said tracking down the men and investigating how the breach occurred are the top priorities for police in the province.

“The escapees have limited options to hide as we know their villages and associates. It is only a matter of time before they are caught and face additional charges,” Harris said.

“I call upon tribal and village leaders to assist us, as many of these same leaders assisted police to arrest these individuals to begin with.”

He urged the escapees to turn themselves in to avoid facing harsher penalties.

“If the escapees surrender, they will likely face lesser penalties than if we have to track them down and arrest them. Surrender is the only lawful path open to them and it is in their own best interest,” Harris said, adding that public safety remains paramount.

Meanwhile, police have also launched an independent internal investigation into the circumstances surrounding the escape and a related public disturbance at the station.

Following the breakout, members of the public entered a restricted area of the Wabag Police Station and caused a disturbance. One person was arrested and charged with obstruction of police duties and refusing to leave police premises.

“If there was misconduct by any police officers, they will be dealt with as the law requires,” Harris said. “An independent investigation was ordered and I have referred the matter directly to the Internal Affairs Division.”

Harris assured the people of Enga that police would act without fear or favour to recapture the escapees and hold those involved accountable.

item.title: Police foil armed robbery along Sepik highway

item.content:encoded:
Effective communication by police in East Sepik has led to the arrest of two armed men who were inside a PMV bus from Wewak that was on its way to Maprik.

East Sepik Provincial Police Commander Superintendent Christopher Tamari confirmed that according to police informants, the two men, who were armed with a homemade gun and a round of live ammunition, were persons of interest who were allegedly involved in robberies along the Sepik Highway.

He said the two men were sighted by members of the public, who quickly reported them to the police in Wewak.

​He said police officers then disseminated the information, including the identity of the bus the suspects were inside, through their police communication channels.

He said police officers from Yangoru quickly responded and blocked off the vehicle along the Sepik Highway between Kubalia and Yangoru, successfully apprehending the two men.

PPC Tamari said the suspects are now detained at the Yangoru police station and will be charged accordingly.

PPC Tamari thanked his members who were quick to respond and encouraged the public to work closely with the police to help protect life and property. He said many criminal activities have been happening along the highway, and this could have been another, but teamwork saved the day.

item.title: Hotel Gilgal creates jobs, gives Mt Hagen a fresh look
item.description: A private investment is transforming the face of Mt Hagen City, with the opening of the multi-million kina Hotel Gilgal, creating more than 80 jobs while boosting confidence in the city's growing business and tourism sector. The new hotel, located in the heart of Mt Hagen City, was officially opened this week after eight years of planning and construction by local businessman and Director of Israe
item.content:encoded:
A private investment is transforming the face of Mt Hagen City, with the opening of the multi-million kina Hotel Gilgal, creating more than 80 jobs while boosting confidence in the city's growing business and tourism sector.

The new hotel, located in the heart of Mt Hagen City, was officially opened this week after eight years of planning and construction by local businessman and Director of Israel Ministry Pastor Michael Onda.

Pastor Onda said the journey to complete the project was challenging, but his vision was to build an international-standard hotel that would provide quality accommodation, create employment and contribute to the development of Western Highlands Province.

"We took eight years to complete this project, and today we are proud to open its doors to the people of Papua New Guinea and our visitors," he said.

The hotel has already employed more than 80 people, providing new job opportunities for local men and women while supporting the province's growing hospitality industry.

Church, business and education leaders who attended the opening described the hotel as a milestone achievement, praising Pastor Onda for investing in his own province and proving that local Papua New Guineans can build world-class facilities.

Former Western Highlands Premier and Chief of the Moge Tribe of Hagen Central, Sir Lucas Roika, said Hotel Gilgal has given Mt Hagen City a new facelift and added value to Papua New Guinea's third city.

"Developments like Hotel Gilgal not only improve the city's appearance but also encourage investment, create employment and strengthen the local economy," said Sir Lucas.

Sir Lucas also appealed to the people of Mt Hagen to put aside tribal differences and protect business investments built by their own people.

He said destroying local businesses discourages development, while protecting them creates opportunities for future generations.

Hotel Gilgal offers executive suites, double and standard rooms, a swimming pool, a fully equipped gym, gaming facilities, three conference rooms, three commercial kitchens, a restaurant and a spacious car park designed to cater for business travellers, tourists and local events.

Pastor Onda also clarified the hotel's operating schedule, saying the business will operate from Sunday to Friday, closing at 6:10 p.m. on Fridays before reopening at 6:10 p.m. on Saturdays.

The opening of Hotel Gilgal marks another milestone for Mt Hagen City, showing how local investment is creating jobs, attracting visitors and helping transform the city into a modern commercial and tourism destination.

item.title: Community leaders calls for stronger values
item.description: Ahi president Bingumalu Ahie has called on parents and communities to guide young people with discipline and responsibility to help build a safer and healthier society. Speaking at a community event in Lae, Morobe, Ahie said discipline should teach children right from wrong so they grow into responsible adults.
item.content:encoded:
Ahi president Bingumalu Ahie has called on parents and communities to guide young people with discipline and responsibility to help build a safer and healthier society.

Speaking at a community event in Lae, Morobe, Ahie said discipline should teach children right from wrong so they grow into responsible adults.

"When we discipline our children in a way that helps them learn, they will understand and take better care of themselves," Ahie said.

He said families, communities and institutions all have a role to play in shaping the behaviour of young people.

Ahie also urged Papua New Guineans to protect the country's social values and work together to keep communities safe and healthy.

"I hope our country understands the importance of the university and the surrounding community working together," he said.

"We will not allow outside influences to dominate our community or damage the wellbeing of our people."

Ahie said communities must stand together to promote respect, responsibility and positive behaviour among young people.

Ahie said lasting change begins at home, with parents, community leaders and institutions working together to raise children with strong values and respect for others.

item.title: SDA youths from PNG and Indonesia team up for evangelism
item.description: Hundreds of young Adventists from Papua New Guinea and Indonesia have teamed up for evangelism in Indonesia for the first time at the recent Arafura International Pathfinder Camporee in Merauke, Indonesia. This historic event marks the beginning of a 5-year partnership between East Indonesian Union Conference and the PNG Union Mission (PNGUM) of the Seventh-day Adventist Church to strengthen evang
item.content:encoded:
Hundreds of young Adventists from Papua New Guinea and Indonesia have teamed up for evangelism in Indonesia for the first time at the recent Arafura International Pathfinder Camporee in Merauke, Indonesia.

This historic event marks the beginning of a 5-year partnership between East Indonesian Union Conference and the PNG Union Mission (PNGUM) of the Seventh-day Adventist Church to strengthen evangelism along the PNG-Indonesian border.

According to the Youth Director for PNGUM Pastor Moses Melua, this partnership provides an unprecedented opportunity for Papua New Guinea Union Mission to mobilize young people for the mission of leading other young people to Christ. He highlighted that this Camporee lays the foundation for ‘Hope Indonesia Evangelism 2030’a national event similar to the recent ‘PNG for Christ’ held in 2024.

The camporee has revealed a strong support from the Indonesian Government through office of the Governor of South Papua Province.

Following the successful event, the 191 delegates from PNG returned to PNG with fond memories, new friendships, and an invitation to attend a similar event in 2028.

item.title: Late Sir Julius Chan honoured with Order of Vanuatu
item.description: Former Prime Minister and founding father, the late Grand Chief Sir Julius Chan, has been recognized by the government and people of Vanuatu with the prestigious Order of Vanuatu, Badge of Distinction. The award recognizes Sir Julius’ historic leadership in deploying the Papua New Guinea Defence Force’s Kumul Force in 1980, which helped liberate Vanuatu and secure its independence.
item.content:encoded:
Former Prime Minister and founding father, the late Grand Chief Sir Julius Chan, has been recognized by the government and people of Vanuatu with the prestigious Order of Vanuatu, Badge of Distinction.

The award recognizes Sir Julius’ historic leadership in deploying the Papua New Guinea Defence Force’s Kumul Force in 1980, which helped liberate Vanuatu and secure its independence.

The award was received on his behalf by his eldest son and New Ireland Governor, Byron Chan, who accompanied Prime Minister James Marape to Port Vila to attend Vanuatu’s 46th Independence Anniversary celebrations.

Governor Chan expressed gratitude on behalf of his family, the People’s Progress Party [PPP], and the people of New Ireland, stating the award as a profound moment of national pride.

"By surprise, I received this honor on behalf of the late Grand Chief Sir Julius Chan, and as his son, I am deeply privileged," Chan said.

"It recognizes and marks all the work Sir Julius did when he was Prime Minister, deploying the Kumul Force to liberate Vanuatu back in 1980. Now, 46 years later, they presented this honor to him.

"They haven't forgotten him; they still remember him. We will carry this award to his final resting place at his tomb and place it near him in recognition of the people of Vanuatu saying thank you for helping them when they were in trouble. Other countries didn't help them, Papua New Guinea alone stepped up."

The presentation took place during official state activities in Port Vila. Prime Minister James Marape was also conferred the Order of Vanuatu alongside Timor-Leste President and Nobel Peace Prize winner José Ramos-Horta.

People's Progress Party national president Brown Sinamoi said the accolade highlighted Sir Julius’ lifelong vision for a unified Melanesia and regional self-reliance.

"Sir Julius worked deeply to encourage the Pacific to work together in unity. Part of that was sending a force into Vanuatu to help bring independence, and subsequently training their special forces," Sinamoi said.

"When their constitution was drafted, they used our Constitution as a model because of their historical split under French and British rule. Out of respect for Sir Julius and his legacy, we thank the government and people of Vanuatu for this recognition."

item.title: Kina Bank cleans NBC studio complex in community service drive
item.description: The Kina Bank Wewak Branch team conducted a major clean-up around the NBC Wewak studio complex as part of its ongoing community service initiatives. Branch Manager Anna Wosley told NBC News this was the bank’s second clean-up, following an earlier exercise along the Wewak Sea Wall Drive
item.content:encoded:
The Kina Bank Wewak Branch team conducted a major clean-up around the NBC Wewak studio complex as part of its ongoing community service initiatives.

Branch Manager Anna Wosley told NBC News this was the bank’s second clean-up, following an earlier exercise along the Wewak Sea Wall Drive

Ms. Wosley said Kina Bank believes that getting to know and supporting communities strengthens community relations, and that giving back through service is one way the bank can contribute.

"The NBC Office is in the heart of Wewak Town, so we decided to get our team to clean around the NBC office," she said.

Staff and their families took part in the clean-up, which included grass cutting, raking, and removal of grass and rubbish. The studio complex was left fully cleaned.

Kina Bank Wewak says it will continue to support more community service initiatives in East Sepik

item.title: Two drown in search for water in Hela
item.description: Two primary school students have tragically drowned in the Koroba-Lake Kopiago district of Hela after a search for drinking water ended in disaster due to the ongoing El Niño drought.
